messages.subject: How should I use ezANOVA() if I already collapsed the data to cell means (i.e., aggregated my data)?
parts:
Hi all,

I want to do a repeated measures ANOVA using ezANOVA() from the ez pacakge. My experimental designs is a two-way repeated measures design: soa (which has four levels: a, b, c, d) X congruency (which has three levels: a, b, c), and the data bellow is organized according to the above order (i.e., soa x congruency, so for example "mrt1" which is the first column after "subject" is the dependent measure for the first level of the independent variable "soa" and the first level of the independent variable "congruency"), with "subject" being the ID column. My question is how should I use ezANOVA() if I already collapsed the data to cell means (the data bellow is after I collapsed the dependent variables for each subject according to soa x congruency. In other words, I'm interested in applying the ezANOVA() on my aggregated data)?

messages.author: dae01c57a3c54a3a
messages.subject: Re: [ez4r] How should I use ezANOVA() if I already collapsed the data to cell means (i.e., aggregated my data)?
parts:
While ez will automatically aggregate data for you if it's not already aggregated, it should be fine if you've already aggregated. However, your data is in the wrong shape; the shape you have is called "wide", whereas ez (and lots of other R packages/functions) expects data to be in "long" format. The "reshape()" function will help reshape it:

    my_long_data = reshape(
        data = my_wide_data
        , direction = 'long'
        , idvar = 'subject'
        , varying = names(a)[2:ncol(a)]
        , v.names = 'mrt'
    )

But then you need to create an "SOA" column and a "Congruency" column, recoded from the numbers in the new "time" column that the above command will create. Work at it for a bit then report back here if you encounter any persistent problems.



--
Mike Lawrence
Graduate Student
Department of Psychology & Neuroscience
Dalhousie University

~ Certainty is (possibly) folly ~
